vscode.web-environments.vite-writes-its-: Vite writes its VITE_ values into the bundle when it builds, so the app is built once per environment, each with its own .env.<name> file.
vscode.web-environments.change-the-build: Change the build default, the output or the commit…
vscode.web-environments.which-environmen: Which environment `smith run build` builds, where the builds go and whether git keeps the .env files.
vscode.web-environments.nothing-is-writt: Nothing is written until you have seen the plan
vscode.web-environments.edit-the-names-l: Edit the names (lowercase words, separated by commas).
vscode.web-environments.built-by-smith-r: built by `smith run build`: what CI and the release build
vscode.web-environments.ci-and-releases-: CI and releases build this one; the others are build:<name>
vscode.web-environments.dist-apps-app-na: dist/apps/<app>/<name> at the workspace root, with every other build
vscode.web-environments.dist-name-inside: dist/<name> inside the app's own folder; smith doctor then accepts it
vscode.web-environments.they-hold-vite-v: they hold VITE_ values, which end up in the browser, so they hold no secret; CI builds with them
vscode.web-environments.each-machine-and: each machine and CI job makes its own .env.<name>; git ignores them
vscode.web-environments.name-at-least-on: Name at least one environment, for example lcl, dev, uat, prd.
vscode.web-environments.is-not-an-enviro: "{name}" is not an environment name: use a lowercase word, for example uat.
vscode.web-environments.cannot-be-an-env: "{name}" cannot be an environment name: Vite or the env files already give it a meaning. Use another word, for example lcl for local.
vscode.web-environments.created-and-igno: created and ignored by git, only .env.example is kept
vscode.web-environments.environments-smi: Environments: {join}; smith run build builds {default}; builds go to {output}; .env files are {files}
